tools.name: search_models
tools.description: Searches the catalogue of AI models and returns their current prices, with a confidence level and the sources backing each price.

tools.name: get_model_price
tools.description: Returns every current price for one model — input, output, cached reads, batch and priority tiers, context brackets — with the confidence level and which sources agree. By default these are the maker's own prices; pass `channel` to get what a reseller charges for the same model instead. Two dimensio

tools.name: compare_models
tools.description: Returns the current prices of several models side by side. Amounts in credits are never converted to money, so a credit-billed model is not comparable to a token-billed one. Two dimensions can share a label, so the ones that would collide carry their qualifiers, e.g. 'Web search (context size: high)

tools.name: price_history
tools.description: Returns a model's price over time. Each point is [date, amount] with the date as YYYY-MM-DD. The series holds only the points where the price CHANGED — prices are step functions, so a stable model is one point, not one per day; when a price changed twice on one day, both points are returned with the

tools.name: recent_changes
tools.description: Lists recent price increases, decreases, additions and removals across the catalogue, newest first.

tools.name: list_providers
tools.description: Lists every provider in the catalogue and how many models each has. These are the houses that MAKE the models: a reseller (Vertex, Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter, a subscription plan) is a sales channel, not a provider — ask `get_model_price` with a `channel` for what one of those charges.

tools.name: data_sources
tools.description: Explains where the prices come from: which sources are consulted, their weight and licence, when each last succeeded, and whether any is currently failing. Use this to judge how much to trust a price.

tools.name: find_tools
tools.description: Searches the full catalogue of available tools by keyword and returns the matching tool names with a short description. Use it when no directly-listed tool fits the task — many tools are available but not listed. Then call tool_schema for the one you picked, and run_tool to execute it.

tools.name: tool_schema
tools.description: Returns the full input schema of a single tool, including which arguments are required. Call it after find_tools and before run_tool.

tools.name: run_tool
tools.description: Executes a tool by name with the given arguments. Use it for tools that are not directly listed — look them up with find_tools and check their arguments with tool_schema first. Prefer a directly-listed tool whenever one fits. If the action is destructive, ask the user to confirm before calling it.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "run_tool" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
